name: libgiconv
reason: No numeric comparison reachable. GNU libiconv (the project behind this lead) is a portability library: its README (read via the gnu-mirror-unofficial/libiconv GitHub mirror) lists supported encodings and makes no speed claim, and its NEWS has no performance numbers. gnu.org is blocked here. Web searches for libiconv versus glibc iconv found only unrelated rows (uclibc-ng's own UTF-8 to wchar rows, a Crystal 'charconv' reimplementation beating the system iconv); libiconv is at most a baseline in other projects' tables, never the faster side.

name: libimagequant
listed_description: Small, portable library for high-quality conversion of RGBA images to 8-bit indexed colour images.
reason: No page with numbers reachable. Opened the README (no speed text), CHANGELOG (self-comparisons only: 'less precise remapping improving speed by 25% in higher speed settings', 'reduced memory usage by further 30%') and the pngquant README (--speed N trade-off, no baseline). pngquant.org, imagemagick.org and jqmagick.imagemagick.org are blocked (EGRESS_BLOCKED). The only baseline claim is a search snippet, 'fast-and-rough speed setting 2.5 to 6 times faster than ImageMagick's current algorithm', from the author's legacy ImageMagick forum thread; it is already catalogued as the wave 10 entry 'pngquant / libimagequant' (https://github.com/kornelski/pngquant, tier C, snippet only), so no second record was written. The only newer numbers found are okooo5km/pngoptim's README (pngoptim 1.69x faster than pngquant), where libimagequant's tool is the slower baseline.

name: libnih
listed_description: Lightweight library of functions and structures.
reason: No numeric comparison anywhere reachable. README states goals (not reimplementing the C library, simple consistent API, D-Bus and expat dependencies) with no performance text; no benchmark directory is documented; the project is a utility/D-Bus helper library, not a speed-oriented replacement.

name: liboqs
reason: No numeric comparison against an outside baseline reachable. README and docs/ (algorithms/, FUZZING.md, PROCEDURES.md) have no benchmark numbers, only the speed_kem, speed_sig and speed_sig_stfl programs; the open-quantum-safe/profiling benchmark repo is archived (June 2025) and its README gives no numbers; openquantumsafe.org is blocked. Search results with numbers are self-comparisons (liboqs AVX-512 versus AVX2, 1.30x to 1.64x, in an Intel builders paper; OQS_DIST_BUILD on versus off) or third-party arXiv papers (blocked) using liboqs as one column. Category guess (concurrency-queues-locks) is wrong; it is a post-quantum crypto library aggregating PQClean and pqcrystals code.

name: libpng
reason: libpng is the incumbent baseline in other projects' tables, not a challenger, so no outside baseline exists. Its own CHANGES file has only self-comparisons: 1.6.36 'Optimized png_do_expand_palette for ARM processors. Improved performance by around 10-22% on a recent ARM Chromebook' (versus earlier libpng), and unquantified SIMD notes (SSE2, NEON, VSX, LoongArch LSX, RISC-V RVV 'improved the performance'); a search snippet gives 20-25% NEON decode gain from a Linaro blueprint (self-comparison, page not opened). README, ANNOUNCE.md, TODO.md and contrib/arm-neon/README carry no numbers; libpng.org is blocked.

name: librb
listed_description: C implementation of ring (circular) buffer, with full thread awareness that allows for concurrent read/write and can automatically grow in size when needed.
reason: No numeric comparison reachable. readme.rst, www/rb_overview.7.rst and the repo tree (rb.c, rb.h.in, tests.c, examples/, man/, www/; no bench directory) contain only 'fast' as an adjective and test-count figures (68,874 tests); librb.bofc.pl is blocked (EGRESS_BLOCKED). No third-party shootout including librb was found.
